# Basic Machining Simulation backend · 0.2.0

A deliberately bounded stock-visualization adapter using the unchanged MIT MillSimSharp core at the revision in `BACKEND.lock.json`. The Floe wrapper source is MPL-2.0; both license texts and the complete pinned upstream archive are retained here. App resources contain only ~50 KB of managed IL/metadata, never a .NET runtime or SDK. These bytes are sent to the explicitly selected external Mac target and are not executable iOS code.

Runtime: arm64 macOS through the **same-Mac** Mac Bridge only. The visible action is **基础加工仿真 / Basic Machining Simulation**. First use runs an ordinary observable `exec.shell` preparation job under existing jobs/environment ownership; it downloads the locked .NET 8.0.33 archive (29,113,192 B), verifies its complete digest and all 188 extracted regular files, then atomically promotes the environment-local cache. `run-basic-machining.sh` verifies both managed resources again before launch. Corruption/missing dependencies fail without choosing a host-installed runtime, Linux guest, temporary environment or another target. No global SDK/install, companion deployment or basic-image change occurs.

This is an App-host domain adapter using existing execution tools, **not a new execution tool or a published Hub Skill**. The current macOS Skill dependency schema handles pip/npm; no invented `dotnet` dependency kind, runtimeComponent allowlist change, reserved publisher identity, unsigned official Skill or hub-ready claim is introduced. Installing the managed resource is a normal task-authorized package command. A future Hub packaging choice must follow the existing signed author/version/dependency protocol; no such publication is required to run this version.

Input `floe.cad-stock-task.v1`: native saved package revision/content/model SHA, four immutable selected-body snapshot members (document, manifest, BRep, native mesh), stable body UUID, owner operation/environment/conversation/run, explicit bounding-box-blank mode and millimetres. Native selection must be one BRep body at identity placement. The selected part is a **reference**, not pre-existing stock or gouge protection. Voxel size is 0.25/0.5/1/2 mm; <=2 million cells; each extent <=1000 mm and coordinates <=10000 mm; cutter radius/length 0.1...100 mm; one XY line <=100 mm at fixed Z. Export <=500000 exposed faces / 1 million triangles / 50 MB. CLI has a 30 s cooperative computation budget; jobs apply a hard 60 s execution limit (240 s preparation).

Output `floe.cad-stock-result.v1` contains original source identity, real runtime/platform/backend SHA and SHA/length of occupancy + binary STL. CLI says `computed-not-job-accepted`; only the App's independently verified real completed owned job may accept it. The native collector rechecks every centre against a separate fixed-Z stadium/cylinder formula and checks stock bounds, volumes, outward normals and closed STL topology. It emits a separate accepted receipt with the actual job/run/environment and complete output digests. Cancellation is fenced before suspension; failure/staleness are sticky, and reopening never replays an old command.

Precision is a centre-sampled voxel mesh. Neither the core's BRep nor an analytic cutting surface is claimed. Rotary sampling's earlier 4-centre miss remains in private qualification evidence; rotary/multi-axis requests are unavailable in this adapter. No G-code, CAM planning, machine/fixture/holder safety, turn-mill or full E38 analysis is delivered.

`build-wrapper.sh` accepts explicit already-managed runtime/compiler/reference/core inputs for a small source rebuild. It does not fetch a compiler or install an SDK. The checked-in App resource ZIP is the qualified pinned artifact; compare source and all output digests before replacing it. Different compiler/source-path settings can produce a different deterministic assembly identity and require updating the resource lock and qualification evidence together.
